items.title: The Three Trainings Open: Brahma's Question, and the Buddha's Threefold Answer

items.zh: 已釋勝義聖教伽他。次當建立意趣義伽他。如經言：一時索訶世界主大梵天王往世尊所，頂禮佛足，退坐一面，以妙伽他而讚請曰：於學到究竟，善斷諸疑網，今請學、所學、修學，為我說。
items.en: The ultimate-meaning verses have now been explained. Next, the verses on essential intent should be established. As the scripture says: at one time, the great Brahmā King, lord of the Sahā world, went to where the Blessed One was, bowed at his feet, withdrew to sit to one side, and with a sublime verse praised him and made this request: "Having reached the very culmination of training, skilfully cutting through every net of doubt — I now ask: what is training, what is to be trained in, and how one should train? Please, teach it to me."

items.zh: 大仙應善聽：學，略有三種，增上戒、心、慧，於彼當修學。
items.en: Great sage, listen well: training, briefly, has three kinds — the higher training in precepts, in mind, and in wisdom. It is in these that one should train.

items.title: Six Supports for Precepts, and How the Three Trainings Actually Unfold

items.zh: 應圓滿六支，四樂住成就，於四各四行，智慧常清淨。初，善住根本，次，樂心寂靜，後，聖見、惡見，相應、不相應。
items.en: One should perfect the six supports, and accomplish the four blissful abidings; with the four aspects applied fourfold to each truth, wisdom becomes ever pure. At first, one dwells well in the root; next, one delights in the mind's own stillness; afterwards, one accords with the noble view and no longer with wrong views.

items.zh: 先淨、樂靜慮，及於諦善巧；即於諸諦中，應生、遠、增長。於諸學處中，有四趣三所。遠離於二趣，於二趣證得。
items.en: First, purity; then delight in meditative absorption; and skill regarding the truths — within these truths, the path should arise, suffering and its origin should be left behind, and cessation should be increased. Within these trainings there are four destinations, [grouped as] three places: two destinations to be abandoned, and two destinations to be attained.

items.zh: 二安住二種，一、能趣涅槃。漸次為因緣，純雜而修習。
items.en: The two abidings [in concentration and wisdom] are of two kinds; one alone leads directly to nirvāṇa; each stage becomes the condition for what follows, whether practised singly or in combination.

items.zh: 最先離惡作，最後樂成滿；諸學是為初，於此學聰叡。由此智修淨，淨生、樂成滿；諸學是為中，於此學聰叡。

items.title: Wisdom's Supremacy, and Which Trainings Share Their Results

items.zh: 從此心解脫，永滅諸戲論；諸學是為尊，於此學聰叡。若行、趣不淨，亦趣於善趣；是行說為初，當知此非共。若行、趣清淨，非諸趣究竟；是行說為中，當知亦非共。若行、趣清淨，於諸趣究竟；是行說為尊。當知此必共。
items.en: From this, the mind is liberated, and all conceptual proliferation is forever extinguished; this training is the most eminent — in this one becomes truly skilled. Where practice leads to impurity, or else to a favourable rebirth, this is called the first practice; know that it shares nothing with the others. Where practice leads to purity, yet not to the ultimate end of any rebirth, this is called the middle practice; know that this too shares nothing with the others. Where practice leads to purity and to the ultimate end of all rebirth, this is called the eminent practice; know that this one necessarily shares in the others.

items.zh: 若有學、無學、當知並聰叡；若有學、無學，當知並愚夫。
items.en: Where there is genuine training and freedom from wrong training, know this together as the truly skilled; where there is wrong training and no genuine training, know this together as the foolish.

items.title: Renunciation, Subtlety, and How the Trainings Combine — The General Overview Closes

items.zh: 若棄捨攝受，亦斷除麁重；及現見所知，是受持三學。若有緣、無緣，亦細、麁顯現。由受持、遠離，言發悟，所引。
items.en: Giving up what one has taken hold of; also cutting off coarse disturbance; and directly seeing what is to be known — this is how the three trainings are undertaken. Having an object or having none; being subtle or being coarsely evident; drawn forth through undertaking a vow, through [bodily and mental] seclusion, and through another's words and awakening [by inner right reflection].

items.zh: 初學、唯有一；第二學、二種；第三學、具三；慧者皆超越。
items.en: The first training has only one; the second training has two; the third training possesses all three — and the wise one surpasses every stage.

blocks.text: The forty-four verses on non-self were the "ultimate meaning". Now come the "verses of intent" (意趣義伽他): fifty-one verses on the **three trainings** (三學) in precepts, mind, and wisdom. Venerable Miào Jìng: "The earlier verses mainly proclaim no-self; the verses below mainly tell you the means to realise it." Today and tomorrow you read the verses; Days 134–135 read the prose commentary, most of which Ru-Yi did not translate. One short pair of verses (0366a05) is also missing from the English.

Brahmā, lord of the Sahā world, praises the Buddha as one who has "reached the culmination of training" and "cut through every net of doubt", and asks: what is training, and how should one train? The Buddha answers: training is of three kinds, the **higher training in precepts** (增上戒學), **in mind** (增上心學, that is, concentration), and **in wisdom** (增上慧學).

subs.head: The means, the order, the purity

items: **Means.** Precepts are perfected through **six supports** (六支); mind through the **four blissful abidings** (the four dhyānas); wisdom through the sixteen aspects of the four truths (impermanence and the rest).

**Order.** "At first, one dwells well in the root": precepts are the root. Venerable Miào Jìng: "Higher mind flows from higher precepts; higher wisdom also flows from higher precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi adds that the reverse is not automatic: with real concentration, precepts are fulfilled; precepts alone do not guarantee concentration.

**Four destinations.** The trainings lead to four destinations: good and bad destinies within the desire realm (from keeping or breaking precepts), the higher realms (from concentration), and nirvāṇa (from wisdom). One leaves the first two and attains the last two. Master Cháng Bǎi: even human and heavenly births in the desire realm are to be left, because "their many objects of desire easily breed karma and obstruct the path".

**Singly or combined.** Beginners practise the trainings one by one; at the middle stage, both singly and together; at the highest, all as one. Venerable Miào Jìng: the middle stage is the stage of application: heat, summit, patience, highest worldly dharma (Day 115).

blocks.text: Precepts alone can bring a good rebirth without the other two: "unshared". Concentration can be attained without wisdom, but not without precepts. Wisdom that ends all destinies never stands without the other two: it is "necessarily shared". Master Cháng Bǎi: in cultivating the cause, concentration depends on precepts alone, not on higher wisdom.

Each training is fulfilled by its own act: precepts by **giving up** what one holds (home and family), concentration by **cutting coarse disturbance**, wisdom by **directly seeing** the truths. Precepts have no object; concentration and wisdom do. The wise one, the arhat, "surpasses every stage".

quiz.q: After the ultimate verses come the verses on intent. How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate the two sets?
options: the former mainly proclaim no-self; these tell you the means to realise it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The earlier verses mainly proclaim no-self; the verses below mainly tell you the means to realise it." Master Cháng Bǎi: the three trainings are the means to realise no-self.

quiz.q: "First one dwells in the root; next the mind's stillness; then noble view." How does Venerable Miào Jìng relate the three trainings?
options: precepts are the root — higher mind and higher wisdom both flow from higher precepts
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Higher mind flows from higher precepts; higher wisdom also flows from higher precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi: with concentration, precepts are fulfilled; precepts don't guarantee concentration.

quiz.q: The English renders 四趣三所 as "four destinations tied to the three trainings." How do the lectures read it?
options: the four are desire-realm good and bad destinies, higher destinies, and nirvāṇa, grouped as three places; both desire-realm destinies are left, the higher and nirvāṇa attained — unrelated to the three trainings
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though human and divine births in the desire realm are good destinies, their many objects of desire easily breed karma and obstruct the path — so they too are to be left.

quiz.q: Of the three stages in "practised singly or in combination," what does Venerable Miào Jìng say the middle stage is?
options: the inner-ordinary stage of application — heat, summit, patience, highest worldly dharma
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The middle stage is the inner-ordinary — the stage of application: heat, summit, patience, highest worldly dharma." The first stage practices singly, the middle both, the highest combined.

quiz.q: The verses call the first practice "not shared," the middle "also not shared," the eminent "necessarily shared." The note says concentration shares nothing with the others. What do the prose and lectures say?
options: concentration "can be accomplished apart from the highest, so it is unshared — but not apart from the first": it shares in precepts, only not in wisdom
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in terms of cultivating the cause, concentration shares in precepts — relying on precepts one attains concentration — but not in higher wisdom. f16 also omits the first two verses on the preconditions.
